A_seams.criterion: blend-band cells where B1 is steeper than R1 + 0.5 and steeper than the core p99 (2.16); failure if any cluster > 0.25 ha
A_seams.b11Cause: Two mechanisms. (1) Too high: the west arm (nw-cape end) and the Vesttind north buttress are still 50-66 m above R1 (locally up to 140 m) where the blend weight falls to 0 at the frozen coast band (coastFreezeM 70 m, coastFeatherM 160 m), so the difference is absorbed in a ~160 m strip and the slope doubles (about 2.5 against R1 1.3-1.6). (2) Too low: at the north-arm headland the carved north cirque and its trough end up to 190 m below R1 just inside the coast feather, so B1 steps up into the frozen R1 cliff. A smaller cluster lies beside the protected windward-gully corridor, where the fjell flank meets the corridor fade.
A_seams.b11VisibleConsequence: Short, over-steep steps where the west arm and the Vesttind north buttress meet the coast: an artificial sea cliff rather than an arm running down to the sea. A raised lip where the north cirque trough meets the frozen R1 cliff at the headland. A steep bank beside the windward gully. All four fail the declared 0.25 ha limit.
A_seams.b2aCorrection: Authored terminal profiles (D1): the authored difference to R1 decays to zero by smoothstep between the 70 m coast freeze and a per-structure terminal length (default 380 m, arm-west 380 m, b-vesttind-north 480 m, arm-north 450 m, C-N 520 m, C-NW 440 m; blended between structures by inverse-square distance), with S1 and S3 protected from the taper; a separate 320 m terminal taper before the windward-gully corridor. Same seam criterion, same 0.25 ha limit.

B_westernCol.b11Cause: At the authored col point the highest authored part is not the west arm (666 m, as designed) but the south-east arm (726 m): that arm starts at the summit, and because the flank-variation branch of ridge_height applied no end caps, the arm continued past its start as a radial cone that still stands 726 m high 250 m west of S0. The smooth-max union keeps it, so the col point is filled to about 729 m. The real low point of the S0-S1 crest moves 100 m west to the arm-west/plateau junction, where the Vestfjell plateau shoulder holds it at 695 m. Vesttind keeps 40 m of prominence instead of the authored 56 m.
B_westernCol.b2aCorrection: South-east arm start cap (30 m, then a 1.6 fall) ends the arm behind the summit; col knot 676 m (target col about 680 m, reconciling the 56 m prominence intent with the achieved Vesttind); Vestfjell plateau start moved to (-935, 2580). Vesttind is not changed; the North Peak apex is unchanged (within 0.1 m inside 25 m), but its west shoulder 25-100 m from the apex is up to 2.3 m lower where the B1.1 spill-over cone is removed.

C_hydrology.lakeAndRiverLevels: unchanged: the water-surface raster is shared with R1 and no terrain under any water cell changed, so every lake level (High Tarn 360 m) and channel bed/water level is as in R1

classification.acceptable authored change: drainage reassignment inside the study area following the new cirques and troughs (the north-coast and central-trough catchments gain, High Tarn loses about 7 ha of its west slope)
classification.defect: none found for sinks or unresolved flow; one dry tarn-site hollow is a representation gap (no water-surface variant), not a drainage failure

peak-ascent.role: primary hiking approach to the Vestfjell shoulder viewpoint

peak-scramble.role: optional alpine summit scramble (viewpoint to North Peak)

D_route.note: Terrain-level cross-slope at +-2 m and +-4 m is the B1.1 metric (unchanged). +-0.75 m and +-1.5 m measure the tread modelled by the B2a bench on the rendered surface. The 4 m heightfield represents the bench with grid nodes, so a 1-2 m tread is only approximated: at switchback interiors the bench is deliberately left out, and there the tread is the original terrain.
